title: Конец войны и роль для Шефа  (End of the War and a Role for the Chef)

segments.t: In the office, Nagiyev angrily orders Vika and Chef Barinov to end the war that is making the entire staff suffer. Afterward, however, the film director approaches Viktor Petrovich and confesses that watching him lose his temper convinced her he is the exact man she needs for her film.
Но, когда вы вышли из себя...
Я поняла это то, что мне нужно.
У вас такие сильные и нежные руки.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'A rare occasion when the old man is actually right.' In Russian, the idea of 'rare' flows naturally into 'right' without extra filler words.
'I am sick and tired of this, Viktoriya.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'for me' before landing on 'Viktoriya'.
'From which the entire staff is suffering.' The grammar packs 'from' and 'staff' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
'Wait, I do not understand, what war?' Max brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'not' in a few short words.
'Alright, guys, that is enough, enough.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'all' and 'kids' in a few short words.
'So let me say this one more time.' The meaning hinges on 'so' working together with 'time' in spoken Russian. Max answers right away.
'Viktoriya, I am addressing you directly.' The grammar packs 'Viktoriya' and 'for you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Kindly make sure that these people.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to take the trouble' before landing on 'these'.
'That the cooks do not wander around the dining room.' The grammar packs 'cooks' and 'hall' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
Но, когда вы вышли из себя...
'But when you lost your temper out there...' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'but' before landing on 'yourself'.
Я поняла это то, что мне нужно.
'I realized that is the exact energy I need.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'I', while 'needs to be' completes the thought.
'You were so expressive.' Vika anchors the line on 'you', while 'such' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
У вас такие сильные и нежные руки.
'You have such strong and gentle hands.' Max chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'hands' to keep a polite distance. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Но, когда вы вышли из себя...
Я поняла это то, что мне нужно.
У вас такие сильные и нежные руки.
When you watch Scene 21 of Episode 19, listen out for the exchange around end of the war and a role for the chef — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
